description: We are 2 northeastern undergrad engineers who are interested in the planning and execution of space missions.
summary: We have developed an interactive game which allows people to plan and execute a moon landing mission. The game focuses on the planning and distribuion of funds as well as overseeing the execution of the physical mission. It provides people with a way to see how funds could be distributed and the down and upsides of each an funding and engineering decision that they had made. This lets someone play around with the funding element of missions and prioritize certain aspects in order to better achieve a mission. It is important because it includes an important issue of space flight which if funding meaning that a person is able to experince the consequences of not spending enough money on a part or spending too much on a certain area.
details: Lunar Launch is a browser game that put a player in charge of a crewed mission to the moon. Players start with $1 billion and a 36 month deadline. The player has to split the budget across NASA hardware then fly the mission. Launch, an asteroid-dodging flight to the Moon, a landing, and a return trip ending in splashdown. Along the way random problems appear that happened on NASA’s Artemis II mission. Players have to deal with the problem with their available resources or suffer mission failure. After each choice the game explains what NASA actually did, with a link to the source. The goal is to show students that mission design is a series of trade offs and managing consequences where cutting one system to save money or time can doom the mission later. We built it with HTML and Java Script(the graphics were made with java script on an html canvas) and CSS in VS Code and then hosted it free on GitHub Pages so it runs in any browser. We also kept it simple so players of any background can learn from it and get interested in nasa missions. This project is creativeas it combines high attention flying and mission planning considerations making your choices in the beginning determine how you need to handle situations in the future. Some factors that our team considered was adding multiple missions however with our skill set wasn't developed enough to take this on to a level we would be satisfied with so we had to only stick to 1 mission.
